_comment: Mutation testing asks a question coverage cannot: do the assertions actually catch a change, or do they merely execute the line? Scoped on purpose — mutating all of src/ runs for hours. These are the pure, branch-heavy modules with the strongest suites, so a surviving mutant here is a genuine gap rather than noise.
_scope: Default scope is the leaf modules — pure, branch-heavy, and NOT imported by half the tree. Breadth is cheap to add on the command line (`npm run test:mutation -- --mutate 'src/utils/helpers/objects.ts'`) and expensive to make the default: `objects.ts`, `props.ts` and `children.ts` are imported almost everywhere, so with perTest analysis nearly all 763 tests cover each of their mutants, which pushed a full run past four hours. Widen deliberately, on a nightly job.
_runtime: A full scoped run is minutes, not seconds — every mutant re-runs the tests that cover it. Treat this as an on-demand or nightly job, not a per-commit gate. `incremental` caches results keyed by mutant, so a rerun only re-tests what changed; delete reports/mutation/stryker-incremental.json to force a cold run.
